project: Report Relay — PowerPoint Report Automation Tool

project_overview.what_it_is: A Streamlit app (app.py) that creates and updates PowerPoint reports from Q-style crosstab Excel files. It parses crosstabs, generates branded charts, and updates existing decks with new data while preserving formatting.
key_workflows: Create New Report: Upload crosstab → configure charts → export PPTX
Update Existing Report: Upload PPTX + crosstab → auto-map shapes to tables → update data in-place

what_was_done_this_session.summary: Major upgrade to the auto-mapping engine. Replaced the manual alt-text-based mapping system with a multi-signal AI fuzzy matching engine that uses value correlation, slide context, series-to-row matching, and time series support.
what_was_done_this_session.problem_solved: The existing system required manual alt-text tagging on every PowerPoint shape to connect charts to crosstab tables. This took too much time for each new project. The upgrade makes mapping automatic and dynamic — it works on any PPTX+crosstab combination without manual setup.
what_was_done_this_session.key_insight: Pearson correlation of chart values vs crosstab values is a 0.9942+ fingerprint even across different data waves. This is the primary matching signal, supplemented by slide text context (Q-codes, question text), series-name-to-row fuzzy matching, and label overlap.

matching_pipeline.description: Multi-signal blended scoring engine in auto_mapper.py
flow: 1. Extract fingerprints from all PPTX shapes (chart categories, series names, values, table headers/rows)
2. Extract slide contexts (question text, chart titles, Q-codes) from text boxes
3. Build column banner pool from all crosstab tables for segment detection
4. For each chart/table shape:
a. Detect chart type: distribution vs segment-breakout vs time-series
b. Value correlation scoring (primary signal, weight 0.45)
c. Label overlap scoring (existing Jaccard/containment, weight 0.25)
d. Slide context scoring (Q-code match + question text fuzzy, weight 0.20)
e. Series-to-row matching (fuzzy series name → row label, weight 0.10)
f. Blend all signals into final score
g. If score >= 0.75: accept match
h. If score 0.40-0.75 and use_llm=True: LLM fallback with enriched context
i. If score < 0.40: unmatched
5. Associate text shapes (question, base, title) via slide context
6. Write alt text onto matched shapes (if confidence >= 0.75)
7. Save PPTX

value_correlation.description: Pearson r between chart values and crosstab values. Works across data waves because the relative pattern persists even when absolute values change.

modes.distribution: Chart values vs table Total column values (aligned by fuzzy-matching category labels to row labels)
modes.segment_breakout: Chart values vs each row's values across banner columns (finds the best table+row combination)
modes.timeseries: Chart values vs each row's values across date columns (normalised date matching)

label_overlap.description: Jaccard overlap + fuzzy containment of chart categories against table row labels (or column labels for flipped charts)

slide_context.description: Q-code extraction from slide text → exact match against table titles. Falls back to SequenceMatcher on question text vs table title.

series_name.description: Fuzzy match of chart series names against table row labels. Handles abbreviations ('Gas too expensive' → 'Gasoline was too expensive') and Top N Box patterns.

matching_pipeline.weight_override: For segment breakout and time series charts, value correlation weight increases to 0.55 and label overlap drops to 0.15 (values are more reliable for these chart types)

chart_type_detection.distribution: Categories are response options (not segment names), series is uninformative ('%%', 'Series 1')
chart_type_detection.segment_breakout: Categories overlap heavily with column banners (Total, Gen Z, etc.), series name is informative (a specific metric)
chart_type_detection.timeseries: Most categories (>=50%%) look like dates (regex patterns for 'Mon YYYY', 'Mon DD-DD, YYYY', etc.)

time_series_update.approach: Append new data points (not full chart replacement)
flow: 1. Read existing chart categories (dates) and normalise to 'mon yyyy'
2. Read crosstab date columns and normalise the same way
3. Find new dates in crosstab not already in chart
4. For each new date, for each chart series:
a. Match series name to table row label (fuzzy)
b. Read the value at that row × date column intersection
5. Call append_chart_point() to add the new category + values to chart XML

test_data.pptx: The State of the American Traveler - March 2026 Report.pptx (80 slides, 30+ charts, zero alt-text)
test_data.crosstab: SATS March 2026 - Internal Crosstab 4 3 2026.xlsx (277 tables across 4 sheets: Demographic Banner, Sheet2, Time Series Banner, Collection Date)

sheets.Demographic Banner: Main cross-tabulations with segments as columns (Total, Gen Z, Millennial, Gen X, Boomer or older, WEST, MIDWEST, NORTHEAST, SOUTH)
sheets.Time Series Banner: Same questions but with monthly date columns (January 2022 through March 2026, ~52 months)
sheets.Collection Date: Small sheet with specific collection date metadata

table_structure.title: Full question text with Q-code, e.g. '(Q1369) 92. Would you say that you (and your household) are better off...'
table_structure.row_labels: Response options (e.g. 'Top 2 Box', 'Much better off', 'Better off', ..., 'Base')
table_structure.col_labels: Segment names or date names, possibly with metric qualifiers like 'Total | 1 or more'
table_structure.values: 2D array of floats (proportions 0-1 for percentages, raw counts for Base)

distribution.description: Horizontal/vertical bar charts with response options as categories and '%%' as series name
distribution.matching_strategy: Categories align to row labels, value correlation against Total column

segment_breakout.description: Charts with segments (Total, Gen Z, etc.) as categories and a specific metric as series name
segment_breakout.matching_strategy: Series name fuzzy-matches to a row label, values correlate across banner columns

timeseries.description: Line charts with dates as categories (66+ data points), tracking metrics over time
timeseries.matching_strategy: Date normalisation + value correlation against Time Series Banner rows
timeseries.update_approach: Append new month data points (chart ends at Feb 2026, crosstab has March 2026)

testing.note: Integration test against the full 80-slide SATS deck + 277-table crosstab was not run due to session time constraints. This is the recommended first test in Cursor.

limitations: Series-to-row text matching is ambiguous when multiple row labels share similar wording (e.g. 'Gas too expensive' scores 0.80 against both 'Travel is too expensive' and 'Gasoline was too expensive'). Value correlation resolves this in practice.
The 'Top N Box' pattern matching is heuristic — it assumes 'or' in a series name → look for Top N Box rows. May need refinement for other composite patterns.
Time series date normalisation handles 'Mon YYYY' and 'Mon DD-DD, YYYY' patterns. Other date formats (ISO, DD/MM/YYYY) are not yet supported.

auto_mapper.py._pearson_r(x, y): Pearson correlation, returns 0.0 if variance is zero or n<3
auto_mapper.py._build_segment_mapping(chart_cats, xtab_: Returns {chart_idx: banner_idx} dict via exact + fuzzy + word-overlap matching
auto_mapper.py._value_correlation_distribution(vals, ca: Returns float 0-1, aligns chart cats to table rows by prefix/fuzzy match
auto_mapper.py._value_correlation_segment(vals, cats, t: Returns (float, matched_row_label), tries every non-base row
auto_mapper.py._value_correlation_timeseries(vals, cats: Returns (float, matched_row_label), normalises dates to 'mon yyyy'
auto_mapper.py._extract_slide_contexts(prs): Returns Dict[slide_idx, SlideContext] for slides with data shapes
auto_mapper.py._series_name_score(series_names, table): Returns (float, matched_row_label), handles Top N Box pattern
Orchestrator — extracts fingerprints + contexts, scores, writes alt text

chart_data_patcher.py.append_chart_point(chart, cat_label, ser: Appends one data point to existing chart XML, preserving all formatting

deck_update.py._update_timeseries_chart(chart, table, r: Finds new date columns, matches series to rows, calls append_chart_point()

auto_mapper.py.WEIGHT_VALUE_CORR: 0.45 — value correlation weight in blended score
auto_mapper.py.HIGH_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD: 0.75 — minimum score to accept a match without LLM
auto_mapper.py.LLM_THRESHOLD: 0.40 — minimum score to trigger LLM fallback
auto_mapper.py.ALT_TEXT_WRITE_THRESHOLD: 0.75 — minimum confidence to write alt text onto shape
